title: Cost-aware trigger sampler and prioritized eval policy for version pin/upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: implement a cost-aware evaluation trigger service that samples requests and orchestrates prioritized eval runs whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded in the catalog or on a customer tenant. Scope includes: trigger policy definitions, sampling strategy, prioritization by tenant risk/profile, resource caps and cost guardrails, and integration points with rollout automation and alerting.

Goals: 
- Ensure every pin/upgrade has an automated quality check that can detect regressions before wider traffic promotion.
- Keep eval costs bounded with a sampling-first approach and budget-aware throttles.
- Prioritize evaluation resources toward high-risk tenants (high-traffic, critical SLA, or flagged by QA).
- Surface deterministic pass/fail signals and confidence scores to rollout automation and SRE dashboards.

Out of scope for initial iteration: full synthetic dataset generation; deep per-tenant human review flow. This ticket focuses on the orchestration and policy layer plus a lightweight sampler and smoke suites.
acceptance_criteria: A trigger rule evaluates and enqueues eval jobs for catalog pin events and tenant-level pin events within 30s of the event
Sampler selects a traffic-representative subset of requests or synthetic probes within configured budget limits
Prioritization rules move high-risk tenant evals to front of queue; low-risk evals run on best-effort capacity
Cost guardrails enforce daily and per-pin quotas; exceeding quota escalates to a k-slimmed smoke-only path
Eval results produce a pass/fail decision and a summarized delta report stored in evals datastore and surfaced to the Console
Rollout automation consumes the pass/fail signal to allow/deny canary promotion and to trigger auto-rollback if configured
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after weekly QA sync. Problem statement: existing pin upgrades are too slow to detect regressions and we have no cost controls for cross-tenant preflight evals.

2026-03-11 - Marco Dubois: Engineering spike completed. Prototype sampler implemented in spike PR #764. Spike shows a 10x cost reduction versus naive full-traffic replay by stratified sampling of top 5 routes.
2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (SRE): Requested hard quotas and an emergency 'smoke-only' fallback route to keep critical tenants protected when eval cluster is saturated.
2026-03-12 - Elena Morales (Design): Reviewed dashboard wireframes. Requested clearer visibility for per-pin budget consumption and per-tenant priority rationale.

2026-03-13 - Marco Dubois: Pushed initial service scaffolding branch (ENG-branch/pin-eval-orch). Implemented trigger listener for catalog events and tenant pin events. Integration points: pub/sub event bus -> trigger service -> eval-queue.
2026-03-13 - Ava Chen: Product review: confirmed prioritization tiers (critical, standard, low) and suggested a heat-score formula combining traffic volume, SLA tier, and recent regression history.

2026-03-14 - Marco Dubois: Implemented configurable cost guardrails with per-day and per-pin budget caps. Added telemetry hooks for budget burn rate to Console. TODO: wire approval gating to rollout automation.
2026-03-14 - QA (Ravi Singh): Drafted smoke suites for catalog-level quick checks; identified three prompt families for safety and hallucination regressions. Need coverage mapping to tenant routes.
Next steps: finalize prioritization heat-score formula, implement confidence-based pass thresholds, add rollout gating hook, and run end-to-end test on staging with two sample tenants.
